title: QUIC RFC 9000 S8P1P4 Retry Token Source Binding and Lifetime Tail
purpose: Describe the focused S8P1P4 closure for Retry token source endpoint continuity, short lifetime validation, and anti-amplification proof after address change.
design_summary: Retry bootstrap tokens are issued by the address-validation token protector with the remote IP address and UDP source port included in the integrity-protected MAC input and an explicit one-minute Retry lifetime. The listener stores the issuing path identity, requires replay Initial packets to carry the exact Retry token, rejects replays from a different remote endpoint before admission, and validates the protected token lifetime before marking Retry replay validation successful. The anti-amplification budget remains the three-times-received-payload cap for unvalidated client addresses.
data_and_state_considerations: The Retry bootstrap state remains listener-local and records the original destination connection ID, Retry source connection ID, Retry token bytes, and issuing remote endpoint. NEW_TOKEN issuance and validation continue to use address-only binding and the protector default lifetime so existing NEW_TOKEN semantics are not widened to source-port continuity or shortened to the Retry bootstrap lifetime. The port-bound token overload is internal and used by the listener Retry bootstrap path.
edge_cases_and_constraints: A Retry replay from the original source address and port is admitted.
A Retry replay carrying the correct token from a fresh UDP source port is rejected before the connection-options callback runs.
Port-bound token validation accepts the exact expiration boundary and rejects the first second after expiration.
Deterministic port mutation fuzzing rejects alternate source ports for the same token.
The anti-amplification budget permits at most three times the bytes received on an unvalidated changed address.
risks: This slice keeps Retry bootstrap state listener-local and does not claim cluster-wide Retry token state.
This slice does not add persistent token secrets across listener restarts.
This slice does not widen public token-management APIs.
This slice does not claim hosted interop readiness.
This slice does not close unrelated deferred fuzz obligations.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the focused S8P1P4 hard proof tail for REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S8P1P4-0003, REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S8P1P4-0007, and REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S8P1P4-0011. It does not claim full token replay hardening beyond the existing listener-local NEW_TOKEN replay cache, public API widening, persistent cross-restart token state, hosted interop readiness, or closure of unrelated deferred fuzz obligations.
